summary: Extraction pass over 16 stored Hong Kong documents (ImmD annual report Appendix 5 for 2013-2023, Chapter 2 for 2020-2023, LegCo LCQ7 of 23 Feb 2011). Adds the earlier-year CIES entry-visa columns repeated in each Appendix 5 (all agree with the earlier reports) and the 2008-2010 average monthly entrants and investment from LCQ7, which match the yearly approval and investment totals in the LCQ12 2010 annex.

observations.location: Reply (c)(i), table of average monthly entrants and investment, row 2008
observations.notes: Average number of CIES 'entrants' per month in the year, as given by the Secretary for Security. The reply does not define 'entrants'; the figures match formal approvals (investment made). Consistent with the LCQ12 (5 May 2010) annex: 1547 approved applicants and HK$11024 million in 2008, i.e. about 129 and HK$0.919 billion a month.

observations.location: Reply (c)(i), table of average monthly entrants and investment, row 2008
observations.notes: Average monthly investment amount (HK$) of CIES entrants in the year, as given in the reply. Consistent with the LCQ12 (5 May 2010) annex: 1547 approved applicants and HK$11024 million in 2008, i.e. about 129 and HK$0.919 billion a month.

observations.location: Reply (c)(i), table of average monthly entrants and investment, row 2009
observations.notes: Average number of CIES 'entrants' per month in the year, as given by the Secretary for Security. The reply does not define 'entrants'; the figures match formal approvals (investment made). Consistent with the LCQ12 (5 May 2010) annex: 2606 approved applicants and HK$18221 million in 2009, i.e. about 217 and HK$1.519 billion a month. The row also prints the change on 2008 (+68% entrants, +65% investment), not recorded separately.

observations.location: Question (c)
observations.quote: the number of applications under the CIES dropped from an average of 570 a month in the first nine months in 2010 to 242 last December
observations.notes: Average applications per month, January-September 2010, stated by the legislator asking the question (Hon Abraham Shek); the government's reply neither confirms nor uses it. Before the 14 Oct 2010 rule change (threshold up to HK$10m, real estate removed).

observations.location: Question (c)
observations.quote: the number of applications under the CIES dropped from an average of 570 a month in the first nine months in 2010 to 242 last December
observations.notes: Applications in December 2010, stated by the legislator asking the question; not confirmed in the government's reply. After the 14 Oct 2010 rule change.

observations.location: Reply (b)(i)&(ii)
observations.quote: real estate investments under the CIES in recent years have only represented about 1% of the value of the total real estate transactions before the amendment
observations.notes: Rounded ('about 1%'); the years covered are not given ('in recent years ... before the amendment' of 14 Oct 2010, when real estate stopped counting). The legislator's question gives the same figure ('around 1%').

new_indicators.name: Programme real-estate purchases as a share of all property transactions
new_indicators.definition: Value of real-estate purchases by programme applicants as a percentage of the value of all real-estate transactions in the country, in a period, as stated by the source.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-hkg (Hong Kong CIES, LegCo LCQ7 of 23 Feb 2011: about 1%).

New CIES paragraph: implemented 1 March 2024, investment of HK$30 million or more in stocks, funds, bonds etc. 'excluding real estate' (not added: the HK$30m threshold and the launch are already recorded from the LegCo brief and InvestHK; this report's 'excluding real estate' differs from the brief, which lets non-residential real estate count for up to HK$10m).

LegCo written reply (23 Feb 2011) on the CIES: question cites applications averaging 570 a month in Jan-Sep 2010 and 242 in Dec 2010, about 1% of property transaction value, and 28 of 2,000 SFC retail funds eligible (press report). Reply: criteria for permissible investment asset classes (five classes of financial assets), reasons for suspending real estate in Oct 2010 and a planned 2013 review, the 70% rule for eligible funds, and a table of average monthly entrants and investment amounts for 2008-2010 with year-on-year changes. All programme numbers extracted; the '28 of 2,000 funds' press figure (a count of eligible products, not a programme outcome) is left as context. The rules described are already covered by existing terms and events.
